description:
Settled with the user 2026-08-24: STOP MAKING DISTINCTIONS BETWEEN MATERIALIZERS. They follow FDB's storage-server pattern — answer if you have the answer, refuse if you don't. Simple. Selection heuristics, rankings and contests are the complexity that pattern exists to avoid.

THE HOLE: nothing tracks whether a materializer actually holds its shard's data, and its absence is not even an event. logic.ex:87 — maybe_load_snapshot(_path, nil), do: :ok. A materializer started for an EXISTING shard with no snapshot available comes up with an empty database and serves reads from it. A read for a key it should have returns 'not found', which is indistinguishable from 'that key does not exist'. It answers a question it does not have the answer to.

FDB DOES NOT ALLOW THIS. A storage server tracks per-shard state locally (storageserver.actor.cpp:470): four mutually exclusive states — notAssigned, adding, moveInShard, readWrite. Readability is exactly one of them:
  bool isReadable() const { return readWrite != nullptr; }   (:558)
A shard that is ASSIGNED BUT STILL FETCHING (adding, fetchComplete not set — :589, :594) is not readable. The refusal happens at the request boundary: 'if (!data->isReadable(req.range)) { req.reply.sendError(wrong_shard_server()); }' (:2994, same pattern :2784). The client retries elsewhere. The server never ranks itself against peers and never guesses; it knows locally whether it finished fetching, and says so.

WHAT THIS DELETES, once we have it:
- The most-advanced-durable CONTEST (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:312-327). Its stated purpose is disambiguating 'empty strays created by earlier failed recovery attempts'. With readability, an empty stray REFUSES the read and recovery asks the next member. No ranking needed. The contest's metric is wrong in principle anyway: durable_version measures stream position, not data completeness — a materializer that starts empty (resume_position = index_manager.current_version = zero) and pulls the log tail climbs in version while holding a fraction of the database, so version can rank an empty replica ABOVE a complete one.
- The INVENT PATH (find_or_create_materializer, :329-343), which manufactures an empty tag-0 materializer on an existing cluster and reads the shard layout out of it. With readability it cannot answer, so the failure is loud instead of silent.

WHAT IT REQUIRES: the party that starts a materializer must say which case it is, because the materializer cannot tell:
- A genuinely NEW shard (fresh cluster's tags 0 and 1; a future split creating a new tag) has no prior data — readable immediately. FDB's seedShardServers.
- A RE-COVER of an existing shard must fetch a baseline before serving — unreadable until it does. FDB's fetchKeys, adding -> readWrite.
Today both go through the same path and both come up readable, which is why the second case is silently wrong.

The baseline source already exists (maybe_load_snapshot / load_snapshot_from_object_storage, logic.ex:86-105) — what is missing is the STATE and the refusal, plus making 'no snapshot for an existing shard' an error rather than a shrug.

READ SEMANTICS: refusal must be its own answer, distinct from an absent key, and classified retryable by clients the way :unavailable already is. Never conflate 'I don't hold this' with 'this key does not exist' — that conflation IS the bug.

SEQUENCING: this precedes bedrock-q67.21.12 and .13. It is the safety mechanism that makes both simple: .12 stops guessing WHO to ask (CoreState names the tag-0 members) and .13 hands data tags to the distributor — but it is readability that makes ASKING safe, and that lets both delete machinery instead of replacing it. P1 because the current behavior can serve an empty result for populated data.
title: A materializer refuses reads for data it does not hold (FDB shard readability)
